text: the probe printed a repair the reader pastes, and its own test handed the words to Command as separate argv rather than to a shell — so the quoting the report depended on was never exercised, and a value holding a space reached git as a value plus a pattern: stored the first word, exited 0, and reprinted the same advice every session after. The harness graded the probe against a shape that could not fail; the fix is that every case now runs the printed command through sh -c from where the session stands

the second reviewer reached the same message from the other side: a hooks directory named a'$(touch pwned)'b made both printed commands execute what the path spelled, because wrapping a path in quotes is not escaping it — the embedded quote closes the literal and what follows is read as shell. The space case had been fixed and mutation-proven one release earlier and the quote case never tried, which is the member-at-a-time rule stated as a defect. Both messages now print every path through printf %q
